hook.text: Banks in trouble can borrow directly from the Fed's discount window.

buildup.text: The discount rate is set slightly above the federal funds rate.

discovery.text: The discount window prevents solvent banks from failing due to temporary cash shortages. It's liquidity insurance.

twist.text: Banks avoid the discount window because markets interpret its use as distress.

climax.text: A safety net nobody wants to use has limited value. The stigma of the discount window undermines its purpose.

punchline.text: Emergency cash available. But using it tells the world your bank is in trouble.

quiz.question: Why do banks avoid using the Fed's discount window?
options: Using it signals financial distress to the market

details.summary: The discount window is the Fed's emergency lending facility where banks can borrow directly from the central bank, but the stigma of using it often prevents banks from accessing help when they need it most.
details.whyItMatters: The discount window is supposed to be the financial system's safety net, but stigma makes it ineffective during crises. Banks fear that borrowing signals weakness, so they avoid the very tool designed to save them.
takeaways: Banks can borrow from the Fed at the discount rate during liquidity stress
Stigma causes banks to avoid the window even when they need liquidity
The Fed created alternative emergency facilities to work around the stigma

faq.question: Why are banks afraid to use the discount window?
faq.answer: Borrowing from the discount window signals that a bank cannot find funding in the private market, suggesting financial trouble. Other banks and investors may then pull their business, turning a temporary liquidity issue into a solvency crisis.

faq.question: How did the Fed address discount window stigma in 2023?
faq.answer: After Silicon Valley Bank's collapse, the Fed created the Bank Term Funding Program offering loans at par value against bank securities. This gave banks a way to access emergency liquidity without the stigma of the discount window.
